clue.text: Escape, grabbing whip and torch

indicators.note: grabbing means the escape word clutches the whip word inside it

parts.note: a flight is an escape, as in taking flight
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: A fugitive bolts, snatching up a whip and a torch on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' signals containment: the escape word wraps round the whip. 'torch' means the hand lamp, not a flaming brand.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a torch is the hand-held battery lamp Americans call by the longer name.

clue.text: Experiences of son supporting discrimination

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: taste is discernment, the ability to discriminate between good and bad

explanation.surface: A son's experiences seem to be propping up some act of prejudice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discrimination' suggests prejudice, but here it is the good sense of discerning taste.
explanation.definitionFit: To get a taste of something is to experience it briefly, so the plural noun matches experiences.

clue.text: Mean to eat mainly raw fish

indicators.note: to eat means the mean word takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: stingy means mean, ungenerous

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone tight-fisted is reduced to eating fish that is mostly uncooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the last letter of 'raw'; 'to eat' signals containment by the mean word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stingray is a flat sea fish with a venomous barbed tail.

clue.text: Bear witness in appointment set tactfully up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
in means the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone gives evidence at a meeting that was arranged with tact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks TSETTA within 'appointmenT SET TActfully'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to testify or vouch for something, the act of a witness.

clue.text: Bishop providing topless pubs and glasses

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
if means providing, as in on condition that

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed, the top of a down entry

parts.note: a local is a person's nearby pub in British usage

explanation.surface: A bishop is scandalised by pubs with topless staff and a pair of glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the L of LOCALS, a British word for one's regular neighbourhood pub, leaving OCALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bifocals are spectacles whose lenses have two parts, for near and distant sight.

clue.text: Black bits found in butcher's mutton

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Dark specks turn up in the meat from the butcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' marks the letters across 'butcheR'S MUTton'.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is soot or a flake of dirt, small black particles.

clue.text: Dependent may see trouble returning during split

indicators.note: during means the next piece happens inside the split word

parts.note: rent means split or torn

indicators.note: returning means the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A dependant may face renewed trouble when a couple separates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' signals a reversal and 'during' containment; 'split' is a past participle used as a noun-like tear here.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliant means relying on something, the same as being dependent on it.

clue.text: Consequences of putting soldiers on the drums succeeded

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the soldiers sit on top of the drums

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are a British army corps
percussion is the drum section of an orchestra
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Soldiers taking over the drums brings repercussions.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British army.
explanation.definitionFit: Repercussions are the after-effects or results that follow an action.

clue.text: Succeed, applying universal rate to most of journey

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
mph, miles per hour, is a rate of speed

explanation.surface: Success comes from applying a uniform speed for most of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' cuts TRIP to TRI; U is the British film certificate for all ages.
explanation.definitionFit: To triumph is to win or prevail, which is to succeed.

clue.text: Strange rote — see enough of different parts

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about rote learning and having had enough of various pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' signals an anagram of ROTE SEE ENOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Heterogeneous describes something made up of diverse, dissimilar elements.

clue.text: Under pressure after spat about verb form

indicators.note: after places the pressure word following the rearranged spat
about means the letters of spat are turned around into a new order

parts.note: tense means under pressure, strained

explanation.surface: Someone feels stressed after a quarrel about grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spat' reads as a quarrel, but 'about' makes it anagram fodder; 'after' orders the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense is the grammatical form of a verb for things already done.

clue.text: Group meet regularly after month

indicators.note: after places the picked letters following the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of meet is taken

explanation.surface: A group gets together at regular intervals once the month is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of MEET.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight, especially of musicians.

clue.text: Levels pitches

definitions.meaning: flattens, as a roller smooths ground or pastry
lurches from side to side, as a ship does in heavy seas

explanation.walkthrough: A groundsman's roller levels a cricket pitch, so the surface hints at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both flattens with a roller and sways like a ship at sea.

clue.text: Muscle resistance seen in retired player

indicators.note: seen in means the resistance letter appears within the other words

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A retired sportsman still shows some resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'player' suggests sport but means a stage actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A retractor is a muscle that draws a body part back in.

clue.text: Parodies efforts to pinch a waistcoat for the Americans

indicators.note: to pinch means to grab, so the efforts word holds the next pieces

parts.note: tries are attempts or efforts
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: Attempts to steal a waistcoat from Americans become a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, so the clue specifies the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque imitation or mockery, much like a parody.

clue.text: Irreligious young lad with no answer needing to be reformed

indicators.note: reformed means re-formed, so these letters must be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A godless youth lacking answers needs to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes the A from YOUNG LAD before the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ungodly means impious or not religious.

clue.text: Immediately and with fatal consequences holding court

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the court abbreviation inside it

parts.note: direly means dreadfully, with terrible consequences

explanation.surface: A court ruling takes effect at once and with fatal results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals that the dire adverb contains the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Directly can mean at once, straight away, as in 'I'll be there directly'.

clue.text: Sucker riding small brown horse

indicators.note: riding means straddling, so the sucker word sits astride the next pieces

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A fool is mounted on a small brown horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding' has MUG straddling S and TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains.

clue.text: Melody dances across street without pretension

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch over the street abbreviation
dances means the letters of the tune word move about

explanation.surface: A tune skips across a road in a humble manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dances' signals an anagram of the tune word, and 'across' has that rearrangement spanning the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Modestly means in a humble, unassuming way.

clue.text: Took off tired, as is confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone departed exhausted and muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' suggests leaving, but means mimicked; 'confused' rearranges TIRED AS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic or lampoon them, which is to satirise.

clue.text: Fairy godmother ultimately enveloped in rancour

indicators.note: enveloped in means that letter is wrapped inside the next word

parts.note: spite is rancour, malice

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fairy godmother turns bitter at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R; 'enveloped in' puts it in SPITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprite is an elf or fairy.

clue.text: Chaste line taken by church article

indicators.note: taken by means the line letter is held inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A church article takes a pure moral line.
explanation.walkthrough: CE stands for the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the sense of morally pure or decent matches chaste.

clue.text: Italian city underpinning church element

indicators.note: in a down clue underpinning means placed beneath the church abbreviation

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: An Italian city forms the foundation of a church element.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is a short form of chromium, a metallic chemical element.

clue.text: Sort of nerve required, seeing credit cut after work

indicators.note: after places the shortened credit word following the work word

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Courage is needed when credit is slashed after an operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims TICK to TIC; 'on tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: The optic nerve carries signals from the eye to the brain.

clue.text: Tie up and hit hard

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a knot is a tie

explanation.surface: Someone is bound and then beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie up' looks like a phrase but 'up' reverses KNOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonk is British slang for hitting a ball or person hard.

clue.text: Rioters rioting about races for coffee

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the races abbreviation
rioting means the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: the TT, Tourist Trophy, are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Rioters run amok over horse races, all for a cup of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' signals an anagram; 'about' wraps it round the Isle of Man motorcycle races abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ristretto is a short, concentrated shot of espresso.

clue.text: Top ticket perhaps requiring time

parts.note: a single is one kind of ticket, a one-way fare

explanation.surface: A top ticket might need time.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a single is a one-way ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A singlet is a sleeveless vest worn as an upper garment.

clue.text: Stickers of Independent politician found during checks

indicators.note: found during means the next pieces sit within the checks word

parts.note: lets are hindrances or checks, as in 'without let'
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An Independent MP turns up during inspections.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpets are shellfish that cling tightly to rocks, hence stickers.
